title: Argument construction is visible
claim: The utility passes an explicit string list to ProcessBuilder and waits for the child process.
witness: Input alpha beta gamma with -n 2 and echo produced two commands/results in a bounded Java 17 run.
repair: The browser exposes argument boundaries as arrays. It previews construction only; it never executes a process.

title: The filter is not a character class
claim: The pattern ;&|><*?$() does not mean 'remove each listed character'. It is valid Java regex syntax but leaves many required characters intact.
witness: Native input alpha;beta & gamma|delta <x> * ? $ (ok) retained the semicolon, ampersand, pipe and other characters. This was a filtering mismatch, not a regex compilation failure.
repair: The revised teaching model uses [;&|><*?$()] to match the assignment list. Argument-list execution is distinct from a shell, and filtering alone is not a complete command-security policy.

title: Empty input with replacement still runs
claim: The replacement branch runs before checking hasInput. -r does not suppress that branch on empty input.
witness: An empty-input Java run with -r -I {} -t echo {} still printed an echo command and a blank result. Without -r, the same branch can also reach the separate default-empty execution.
repair: Check the empty-input policy before either batching or replacement. The revised model does so.

title: Blank lines and batch limits need rules
claim: The main reader stops at the first blank line. -n is parsed without a positive-range check; zero can prevent loop progress. Helper variants also have command-argument parsing differences.
witness: alpha, then a blank line, then beta: the archived reader never reaches beta. The browser refuses n≤0 rather than running a nonterminating branch.
repair: The revised reference reads to EOF, validates n, and keeps fixed arguments distinct. The variants are archived without an invented final-version order.

title: Public class names and source launch
source: TCP work/*.java; New folder/help.java, helper.java, X.java
claim: Several archive filenames differ from their public class names. Ordinary javac compilation expects matching filenames.
witness: All eight source texts compiled using Java 17 in isolated directories after copies were named for their public class. The originals were not renamed or modified.
repair: Use TCPClient.java, TCPServer.java or MyXargs.java for separate local compilation copies. Isolate the two HTTP variants because both define HttpRequestHandler. Compilation is not an end-to-end network test.

title: Chat relay excludes the sender
claim: The source checks handler != this. Messages go to registered peers, while join/leave information is written to the server console rather than broadcast to clients.
witness: With Alice and Bob, Alice's message appears in Bob's received inbox. Alice's received inbox has no server echo in the source model.
repair: Keep this behavior visible. The revised reference adds explicit join/leave notifications, labeled as new behavior.

title: Duplicate names break registry ownership
claim: A second client with the same username replaces the map entry. The old handler can later remove the newer handler's entry by name.
witness: Connect two clients named Alex, then disconnect the older client: the registry can lose the active newer client. The source-behavior model demonstrates the issue deterministically.
repair: Atomically reserve unique names and remove only the matching handler, e.g. putIfAbsent and remove(name, this). A full server also needs serialized writes and bounded resource management.

title: Shutdown notes exceed the implementation
source: TCP work/tcpcss.java; TCP Client Code Overview and Steps.docx
claim: Changing running does not by itself unblock ServerSocket.accept(), readLine() or Scanner.nextLine(). ConcurrentHashMap also does not make compound lifecycle or stream writes automatically safe.
witness: The server hook sets a flag but does not explicitly close the listening socket or drain handlers. A null username can also reach remove(null), which ConcurrentHashMap does not permit.
repair: Close blocking resources deliberately, track ownership, handle EOF/null, and test cleanup under real connections. No complete native shutdown/network integration pass is claimed here.

title: A 404 body needs a 404 status
claim: The route handler always emits HTTP/1.1 200 OK, even when its body says 404. Substring tests also let /hello-extra match /hello.
witness: The early route model returns 200 for GET /missing and for a POST line containing /hello.
repair: The reference validates the method and selects exact resources/statuses. This model is illustrative; it does not execute the Java listener.

title: Path boundaries are segments
claim: String.startsWith(baseCanonical) can accept a sibling directory whose name begins with the root name. startsWith(GET) also admits a non-GET token beginning with GET.
witness: A fictitious /demo/webroot-backup sibling passes a /demo/webroot string-prefix test. The request desk uses only a synthetic sibling fixture to illustrate this boundary.
repair: Use normalized/canonical Path segment containment and exact method parsing, with a deliberate URL-decoding policy. The new reference rejects attempts to escape its synthetic root.

title: One pool per connection is not a shared pool
claim: Each accepted connection creates another cached thread-pool executor. The code does not retain/shut down these executors as a shared bounded resource.
witness: Executors.newCachedThreadPool() occurs inside each accept loop. This is a source inspection, not a stress-test measurement.
repair: Create one bounded executor outside the loop, submit handlers to it and close it during shutdown. The browser's event diagram is conceptual, not a scheduler benchmark.

title: Bytes, text and HTTPS are separate concerns
claim: DataOutputStream.writeBytes writes low-order bytes, and String.length counts UTF-16 units. These are not general UTF-8 framing. The file-serving branch correctly uses the byte-array length for file responses.
witness: The new reference uses TextEncoder for response byte lengths. The archived chat is shown with printable ASCII input to avoid pretending its Unicode transport is correct.
repair: Use an explicit charset and count encoded bytes. HTTPS configuration alone does not prove client trust; the browser performs no TLS handshake and includes no private keystore or certificate files.

title: Captures are evidence, not invented lab conclusions
claim: 189 and 11,639 enhanced packet blocks were parsed and exported as anonymized header metadata. No separate lab worksheet or submitted capture analysis was identified.
witness: The observatory shows all packet counts, relative times and protocol breakdowns. IPv6 extension headers are not decoded, and port numbers do not prove application protocol.
repair: Use endpoint aliases and hide payloads/absolute timestamps. Preserve books, study guides and lecture material as references, separate from original project code.
